flawed_step: After Euler's formula (n - e + f = 2) and the face-count bound 2e >= g*f (which give e <= g(n-2)/(g-2)), reaching e <= 5(n-2)/3 needs girth g >= 5, i.e. every face bounded by at least 5 edges. The hypotheses (simple, planar, connected, has a cycle) only guarantee g >= 3, which gives just e <= 3n - 6. So this step cannot be justified, and the claim is in fact false.
counterexample: Triangle K3: n = 3, e = 3. It is connected, simple, planar and contains a cycle. The claimed bound is (5*3 - 10)/3 = 5/3 < 3 = e. Also K4 (planar): n = 4, e = 6 > 10/3.
assessment_summary: The bound (5n-10)/3 holds only for planar graphs of girth at least 5. With triangles allowed, K3 (3 edges > 5/3) and K4 (6 edges > 10/3) break it. The proof attempt fails at the step that needs every face to have length at least 5.
